strengths: Using LLMs to extract parameters for building SNNs is an interesting topic.
The project aims to tackle relevant research questions.
The use of open source LLMs ensures wider applicability of the method.
The conclusions does acknowledge some limitations of the work.
Using LLM to automatically build and update knowledge graphs from unstructured data.
Organizing complex experimental data in neuroscience and converting them into computable models.
Both areas are very interesting and have practical application value.

Knowledge graphs are difficult to be expanded to a larger scale, updated and deployed in real time due to their high construction and maintenance costs; graph databases provide a reliable way to store and reason about complex information.
Knowledge graphs can benefit from LLM's powerful natural language parsing capabilities, and LLM can benefit from knowledge graphs' reliable information storage methods to alleviate hallucinations.
There is a large GAP between current AI research and neuroscience research; researchers in the two fields find it difficult to communicate using the same academic language.
A large number of experimental results produced in neuroscience research are difficult to be converted into clear and reusable computational models in the field of machine learning.
Advanced machine learning models (such as LLM, LVM) lack biological interpretability, and it is difficult to find corresponding experimental evidence in neuroscience.
Bridging this GAP in any way will help the two fields communicate and benefit each other.
